x: Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner.
Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.

What is it about men like Firth, Driver, Pirie and company which enables them always to strike the front within half a mile or so? Pat Newell, running in his first cross country race this season, clung tenaciously to a good start and was always placed around the forty mark.
Firth and Driver who finished 4th and 2nd in the English 'National' could only manage 52nd and 60th and it was left to Perkins 34th and reserve Humphreys 39th to complete the six.
